stories.title: Municipal Credit Union Signs 6K-SF Lease for New Branch at 162-15 Jamaica Avenue
stories.excerpt: Municipal Credit Union (MCU) has signed a lease to open a new retail branch in Jamaica, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. The not-for-profit credit union, which has locations citywide and caters only to New York City residents, signed a 15-year, roughly 6,000-square-foot lease at Michael Rosilio’s 162-15 Jamaica Avenue, according to landlord broker Augenbaum Realty. Asking rent for the ground-floor space in Jamaica’s business district was more than $100 per square foot, according to the brokerage. Josh Augenbaum and Murray Mizrachi of Augenbaum Realty represented the landlord in the transaction, while Jordan Kaplan of CBRE negotiated on behalf of the tenant. “Ownership is pleased to have provided a beautiful wide-open space on a super busy corridor where Municipal Credit Union will provide their customers with a state of the art banking experience,” Augenbaum said in a statement. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The adjacent spaces in the building were recently leased to an Olgam Life plasma donation center and a Cold Stone Creamery, which still had signage up as recently as June, Google images show. A 25,000-square-foot Fitness Factory also signed a lease in the same building at 162-11 Jamaica Avenue, also owned by the Rosilio family and brokered by Augenbaum Realty, The Real Deal reported in July. The Rosilio family purchased the property in November 2024 for $10.5 million from Ruben Azrak. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Municipal Credit Union signed 15-year, 6K-SF lease at 162-15 Jamaica Avenue, Queens.
Ground-floor asking rent exceeded $100/SF in Jamaica's business district.
Retail anchors (plasma center, Cold Stone) recently leased adjacent spaces in building.
stories.summary: A not-for-profit credit union catering to NYC residents leased 6,000 SF on the ground floor of 162-15 Jamaica Avenue in Jamaica, Queens, for 15 years at over $100/SF. The transaction signals sustained retail demand and tenant confidence in the Jamaica corridor, with complementary tenants (donation center, ice cream) recently securing space in the same building. The lease demonstrates stability in neighborhood-serving retail despite broader office and retail headwinds.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, retail stabilization and ground-floor activation in Jamaica, Queens can support mixed-use and transit-oriented multifamily projects in the submarket by improving pedestrian appeal and neighborhood amenities, which support rents and absorption.

stories.title: Multifamily Developer LCOR Buys Taconic’s UES Life Sciences Site for $73M
stories.excerpt: Taconic Partners has parted with another life sciences project in Manhattan. The developer sold 309 East 94th Street on the Upper East Side for $73 million, according to city records filed Thursday. The buyer, LCOR, develops multifamily properties along the East Coast and recently entered South Florida’s residential market. The sale of the 87,000-square-foot assemblage between First and Second avenues marks a slight premium on the $70 million all-cash deal that last transferred the site from the Karten family to Taconic and its joint venture partners in December 2021. The joint venture, composed of Taconic subsidiary Elevate Research Properties, Nuveen Real Estate and Flatiron Equities, planned to construct a 200,000-square-foot, Class A research lab. The eight-story Iron Horse Labs was designed to benefit from proximity to major academic medical institutions Rockefeller University, Mount Sinai Medical Center and NYC Health + Hospitals. The project secured a $79 million construction loan from Ares Commercial Real Estate in 2022 and began construction in 2023, but its current progress is uncertain. The site still contains a five-story loft-style building, a two-story garage and an auto shop, according to The Real Deal. The Upper East Side deal follows Taconic’s $188 million sale of West End Labs at 125 West End Avenue in July. That asset, part of Taconic’s 3.4-acre West End Campus, was acquired by Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square Foundation. The life sciences sector continues to navigate post-pandemic vacancies. Leasing volume for New York City’s life sciences sector fell 84 percent in the first three months of 2026 compared to the previous quarter, according to CBRE data. It’s unclear who brokered the sale at 309 East 94th Street. Spokespeople for Taconic and LCOR did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: LCOR acquired 87K-SF UES site (309 E. 94th St.) from Taconic for $73M, slight premium over 2021 basis.
Taconic abandoned planned 200K-SF Class A life sciences project (Iron Horse Labs); $79M Ares construction loan likely abandoned.
LCOR plans multifamily redevelopment; East Coast developer expanding into South Florida residential.
stories.summary: LCOR, an East Coast multifamily developer, purchased a 87,000-SF assemblage on the Upper East Side from Taconic Partners for $73 million. Taconic had acquired the site in late 2021 with plans to develop Iron Horse Labs, a 200,000-SF research facility targeting Rockefeller University, Mount Sinai, and NYC Health + Hospitals as tenants. LCOR's purchase signals an exit from life sciences development in Manhattan and a pivot back to multifamily, likely reflecting softness in lab/research demand and developer confidence in residential returns on the UES.
stories.impact: LCOR's move into the UES with multifamily signals apartment developers are acquiring and repositioning sites previously earmarked for life sciences, reflecting weaker lab demand post-COVID and persistent residential strength on Manhattan's Upper East Side. This creates supply-side relief for existing multifamily assets and validates continued multifamily underwriting in prestige submarkets, even as alternative-use projects stall.

stories.title: CRE Finance Council Names Paul Vanderslice New CEO
stories.excerpt: The CRE Finance Council has turned to a commercial real estate banking veteran as its next leader. The leading trade organization for commercial real estate finance professionals announced Friday morning that Paul Vanderslice, who has led BMO’s commercial mortgage-backed securities platform for the last six years, will be assuming the role of president and CEO effective Sept. 30. He will replace Lisa Pendergast, who retired in August after 10 years leading CREFC. Vanderslice’s new role leading CREFC will also mean his departure from BMO with his last day there scheduled for Sept. 29. Prior to joining BMO Capital Markets in 2020, Vanderslice held senior leadership roles in CRE finance at CCRE and Citigroup. He has been a CREFC member for nearly three decades, including a stint as chair of both the group’s executive committee and board of governors from 2012 to 2013. “Paul brings deep industry expertise, a longstanding commitment to CREFC, and a clear understanding of the issues and opportunities facing our members,” Toby Cobb, co-founder and co-managing partner of 3650 Capital and chair of CREFC’s executive committee and board of governors, said in a statement. “Having previously served as chair and as a current member of the board of governors, Paul knows the organization and the industry exceptionally well. We look forward to his leadership as we enter this next chapter.” Vanderslice joined BMO Capital Markets, a subsidiary of Bank of Montreal, in September 2020 to launch and lead the bank’s CMBS platform after spending two years as CEO of CCRE. He spent more than 30 years at Citigroup, where he helped build up the bank’s CMBS business. Leland Bunch, chair of CREFC’s CEO search committee and managing director at Bank of America, said a number of candidates were considered from across the CRE industry and leasing U.S. trade associations. “Paul distinguished himself through his lifelong commitment to commercial real estate and his longstanding dedication to CREFC,” B
bullets: Paul Vanderslice, BMO CMBS platform lead for 6 years, becomes CRE Finance Council CEO Sept. 30.
Vanderslice replacing Lisa Pendergast after 10-year tenure; brings 30-year CREFC membership and banking pedigree.
Leadership change at key CRE finance trade body as market navigates SOFR transition and capital conditions.
stories.summary: The CRE Finance Council appointed Paul Vanderslice, former head of BMO's commercial mortgage-backed securities platform, as president and CEO effective September 30, replacing Lisa Pendergast. Vanderslice brings nearly three decades of CREFC membership and prior senior roles at CCRE and Citigroup. His appointment reflects the organization's commitment to deep industry expertise during a period of shifting capital markets and financing structures.
stories.impact: Organizational leadership shifts at CREFC have limited direct bearing on development feasibility, but Vanderslice's deep CMBS platform experience may signal the council's focus on CMBS market stabilization and capital availability—key factors for multifamily bridge and permanent financing. Monitor for CREFC advocacy on rate/spread environment and credit availability, which directly affect development underwriting and exit strategies.

stories.title: Harbor Fitness to Open 20K-SF Club at 3460 Nostrand Avenue in South Brooklyn
stories.excerpt: Harbor Fitness has signed a lease for its eighth location in Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The Brooklyn-based fitness brand signed a 25-year, 20,000-square-foot lease at Gaama Partners’ 3460 Nostrand Avenue, according to broker Augenbaum Realty. The space was divided evenly between the first floor and the lower level of the property in Sheepshead Bay, Brooklyn. Asking rent for the space was $40 per square foot, according to the brokerage. Josh Augenbaum of Augenbaum Realty represented both the landlord and tenant in the deal. “This will service the Sheepshead Bay community fully with state-of-the-art equipment and knowledgeable staff like all Harbor Fitness locations have,” Augenbaum said in a statement. Augenbaum has worked with Harbor Fitness before, helping the brand establish its 26,000-square-foot sixth location at 943 Kings Highway in Midwood, Brooklyn, in 2021. He said the relationship began with a cold call. Harbor Fitness’ newest Sheepshead Bay club will also feature a 6,000-square-foot outdoor space. The fitness brand did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The single-story property at 3460 Nostrand Avenue was previously owned and occupied by children’s ​​clothing, toys and accessories retailer S&D Kids, which has a remaining location at 1480 Rockaway Parkway in Canarsie. The building was listed for sale in early August 2025. Gaama Partners, which shares a mailing address with Augenbaum Realty, bought it for $5.1 million on Sept. 1 of this year, according to property records. The Harbor Fitness lease was also signed Sept. 1, according to Augenbaum Realty. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Harbor Fitness signed 25-year, 20K-SF lease (8th Brooklyn location) at 3460 Nostrand Ave, Sheepshead Bay.
Asking rent $40/SF; space split evenly between ground floor and lower level; includes 6K-SF outdoor amenity.
Brooklyn fitness operator expanding locally (6th location opened Kings Highway in 2021); demonstrates fitness-anchor demand stability.
stories.summary: Harbor Fitness, a Brooklyn-based fitness brand, leased 20,000 SF across two levels at 3460 Nostrand Avenue in Sheepshead Bay for 25 years at $40/SF. The space features a 6,000-SF outdoor area. This is Harbor Fitness's eighth Brooklyn location and reflects sustained demand for fitness anchors in outer-borough neighborhoods. The operator previously established its sixth location at 943 Kings Highway (Midwood) in 2021.
stories.impact: Fitness-anchor confidence in outer-borough commercial corridors (Sheepshead Bay, Midwood) can support mixed-use and multifamily projects that benefit from ground-floor retail activation and neighborhood amenity density. Long-term fitness leases at $40/SF signal landlord/investor appetite for well-located neighborhood retail, reducing vacancy risk for multifamily podium or ground-floor retail components in similar Brooklyn submarkets.

stories.title: Data Center Supplier to Spend $1B on Charlotte-Area Factory Expansion
stories.excerpt: Prysmian North America, a leading provider of solutions for energy and digital connections, is spending over $1 billion on its factory expansion in Catawba County. The 900,000-square-foot addition to the Claremont facility will create more than 385 new jobs. Claremont is 15 miles from Charlotte. The expansion, which includes a new glass manufacturing facility, additional cable production capacity, and an expanded research and development center, is expected to be complete by 2030. Prysmian, the Milan-headquartered parent company of Prysmian North America, is the world’s largest manufacturer of cables and systems for energy and telecommunications. The plant produces the fiber-optic cable that underpins broadband expansion, 5G and 6G networks, and the high-capacity digital infrastructure driving nationwide demand for connectivity. The company is a key supplier to the data center industry. The post Data Center Supplier to Spend $1B on Charlotte-Area Factory Expansion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Prysmian North America investing $1B+ in 900K-SF factory expansion, Claremont, NC (Catawba County, 15 miles south of Charlotte).
Expansion adds 385+ jobs; includes glass manufacturing, cable production, R&D; completion by 2030.
Prysmian supplies fiber-optic cable for broadband, 5G/6G, and data center infrastructure; major supply-chain play for digital connectivity.
stories.summary: Prysmian North America, world's largest cable and energy systems manufacturer, is committing over $1 billion to expand its Claremont, North Carolina facility (15 miles from Charlotte) by 900,000 SF. The expansion will create 385+ new jobs and include glass manufacturing, additional cable production capacity, and an expanded R&D center, with completion targeted for 2030. Prysmian is a key supplier of fiber-optic cable underpinning broadband, 5G/6G, and data center buildouts.
stories.impact: Major employer expansion 15 miles south of Charlotte signals sustained industrial/manufacturing job growth in the Charlotte metro, driving in-migration demand for workforce housing. Multifamily developers should monitor absorption and rent trajectory in Charlotte and nearby submarkets (Concord, Kannapolis corridor) as manufacturing jobs and wages support middle-income apartment demand. This is a long-cycle signal (2030 completion), but positions developers to acquire/entitle projects in the Charlotte industrial corridor now.

stories.title: Evolve Inks $70M Construction Loan for Palm Coast Apartments
stories.excerpt: Evolve Companies closed on a $70 million bridge and construction loan for a 352-unit multifamily development at 4800 US Hwy. 1 N. in Palm Coast, Florida. Northmarq’s West Palm Beach Debt + Equity team, led by Chris Hammel, arranged the loan on behalf of the borrower with Cross Harbor Capital Partners’ involvement. The loan was non-recourse financing that recapitalized phase I’s construction loan and preferred equity and funds for phase II’s construction. Evolve Palm Coast features luxury one-, two-, and three-bedroom floor plans with private patios/ balconies. Community amenities include a pool with a lounge and outdoor kitchens, fire pits, a golf simulator, a co-working space, a full gym with a yoga studio, a dog park and a pet spa. Earlier this year, Northmarq and Cross Harbor also arranged construction financing for Evolve Companies’ Evolve Crossing, a Class A multifamily development in Burlington, North Carolina. The post Evolve Inks $70M Construction Loan for Palm Coast Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Evolve Companies closed $70M bridge and construction loan for 352-unit luxury multifamily, Palm Coast, FL (US Hwy 1 N).
Northmarq/Cross Harbor arranged non-recourse financing recapitalizing Phase I and funding Phase II construction.
Evolve Palm Coast: one-, two-, three-bed units with premium amenities (pool, golf sim, co-working, dog spa, yoga).
stories.summary: Evolve Companies secured a $70 million bridge and construction loan for Evolve Palm Coast, a 352-unit luxury multifamily development at 4800 US Highway 1 North in Palm Coast, Florida. The Northmarq/Cross Harbor non-recourse financing recapitalized Phase I's existing construction loan and preferred equity and funds Phase II construction. The project features premium one-, two-, and three-bedroom units with extensive amenities including pool, golf simulator, co-working space, gym, yoga studio, dog park, and pet spa.
stories.impact: Lender appetite for multifamily construction financing in Palm Coast and Florida's I-95 corridor remains strong, signaling investor confidence in leisure/retiree and workforce housing demand. Palm Coast's growth (population influx, job availability) supports mid-market multifamily fundamentals; developers should monitor Phase II absorption and rent trajectory to gauge feasibility of additional projects in the coastal Florida market.

stories.title: Investor Group Picks Up 192K-SF Sandy Springs Office Park
stories.excerpt: Ardent Properties traded the Century Springs Office Park in Sandy Springs for $20.75 million. The 192,247-square-foot, two-building infill office property is in the Central Perimeter submarket Newmark Capital Markets Jay O’Meara, Justin Parsonnet and Ryan Reethof represented the The Ardent Companies in the transaction. A partnership between OA Development and Buligo Capital Partners acquired the property. Ardent acquired the asset in 2014. Century Springs marks OA’s fourth recent office acquisition, increasing their portfolio to more than 2 million square feet. Century Springs consists of two mid-rise office buildings and has maintained average occupancy above 90% over the past decade. The asset is poised to benefit from the completion of the neighboring Hillcrest mixed-use development, and walkability to City Springs, Parkside Shops, and other surrounding amenities. The post Investor Group Picks Up 192K-SF Sandy Springs Office Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: OA Development and Buligo Capital acquired Century Springs Office Park, Sandy Springs, for $20.75M (192K SF, 2 buildings).
Ardent Properties held asset since 2014; maintained >90% occupancy over past decade in Central Perimeter submarket.
OA's fourth recent office acquisition; portfolio now exceeds 2M SF; asset positioned to benefit from neighboring Hillcrest mixed-use development.
stories.summary: A partnership between OA Development and Buligo Capital Partners acquired Century Springs Office Park in Sandy Springs for $20.75 million. The 192,247-SF, two-building infill office property in the Central Perimeter submarket was held by Ardent Properties since 2014 and maintained average occupancy above 90%. The acquisition marks OA's fourth recent office deal, bringing their portfolio to over 2 million SF. The asset is positioned to benefit from the nearby Hillcrest mixed-use development.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, OA's aggressive office acquisition strategy in Central Perimeter/Sandy Springs and portfolio scale (2M+ SF) may indicate confidence in Atlanta's office-to-residential conversion potential or submarket stabilization. Monitor for conversion/redevelopment signals from OA or similar developers, which could compress office cap rates and limit multifamily land availability in high-barrier Central Perimeter submarkets.

stories.title: Consumer Prices Rise 0.4% in August as Gasoline Costs Accelerate
stories.excerpt: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in August, accelerating from a 0.1% gain in July as gasoline and other energy costs lifted household expenses, the Labor Department reported Friday. The Consumer Price Index increased 3.4% over the 12 months through August, matching July’s annual pace. Excluding volatile food and energy components, core CPI rose 0.3% for the month, following a 0.2% increase in July. Core prices were up 2.4% from a year earlier, easing from a 2.5% annual increase in July. Gasoline was the largest contributor to the August increase. The gasoline index climbed 3.9%, accounting for more than one-third of the monthly advance in the overall CPI. The broader energy index rose 2.1% during the month. Over the past year, energy prices increased 16.3%, largely reflecting a 27.4% increase in gasoline prices. The sharp rise in fuel costs has been a principal source of renewed headline inflation pressure, even as the underlying inflation rate has moderated. Shelter costs, a closely watched category because of their large weight in the CPI, rose 0.3% after a 0.1% increase in July. Food prices increased 0.1%, with food away from home rising 0.3%. Other categories recording monthly gains included communication, lodging away from home, airline fares, education, and used cars and trucks. The post Consumer Prices Rise 0.4% in August as Gasoline Costs Accelerate appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: U.S. Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in August, 3.4% year-over-year; core CPI +0.3% monthly, +2.4% annually.
Gasoline index climbed 3.9% (largest contributor); broader energy up 2.1%; 12-month energy prices up 16.3%.
Shelter costs rose 0.3% monthly; food away from home +0.3%; inflation moderating but energy-driven volatility persists.
stories.summary: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in August (3.4% year-over-year), accelerating from 0.1% in July, driven primarily by a 3.9% surge in gasoline prices, which accounted for more than one-third of the monthly CPI advance. Core inflation (excluding food and energy) rose 0.3% monthly and 2.4% annually, easing from 2.5% a year earlier. Shelter costs, a key housing-related metric, increased 0.3% after a 0.1% gain in July.
stories.impact: Rising energy and shelter costs support housing inflation narrative and may constrain renter purchasing power and multihousing demand in price-sensitive markets. However, moderating core inflation (2.4% YoY) and near-target trend suggest Federal Reserve may pause or cut rates in coming quarters, potentially lowering multifamily financing costs and improving development feasibility. Monitor shelter cost acceleration—if sustained, could pressure rent growth assumptions and occupancy in middle-income/workforce housing segments.

stories.title: Report: Tariffs Won’t Impact Every U.S. Market in the Same Way
stories.excerpt: Tariff discussions between Canada and the United States have been fractious, to say the least. As of this writing, Canada has issued retaliatory tariffs totaling more than $20 billion on U.S. imports in response to Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods that were formerly tariff-free under CUSMA. While exposure remains a concern, Cushman & Wakefield said it is uneven across the United States. In its recently released report, “The Scale of It All: Updates on the Most Recent U.S.-Canada Tariffs,” Cushman & Wakefield measured the location quotient (LQ) of tariff-weighted bilateral imports based on their composition versus overall import volume. The result? “States like Maryland, Kentucky, Texas and Michigan have tariff-related exposures well above the North American average,” the report said. The reason is that the states’ import mix relies on heavily tariffed products, including automotive and vehicle parts in Michigan and Texas and aluminum products in Kentucky and Maryland. However, that exposure isn’t necessarily weighing down the states’ economies. Trade accounts for 0.6% of Maryland’s gross domestic product and 1.5% of Texas’ GDP. At the same time, “many Canadian provinces have lower tariff-weighted exposure, but trade with the U.S. represents a much larger share of their economies,” according to the report. What It Means for CRE The uneven exposure could have several implications for commercial real estate. More 3PL demand. Third-party logistics companies could experience increased volume as retailers, wholesalers and manufacturers respond to tariffs with just-in-case (JIC) strategies designed to create inventory buffers. Bonded warehouse demand. Companies could rely on bonded warehouse strategies to delay tariff payments, even as available bonded warehouse space has been limited since last year. More onshoring. bullets: Canada issued $20B+ in retaliatory tariffs on U.S. imports; exposure uneven across states.
States with high tariff exposure: Maryland, Kentucky, Texas, Michigan (automotive, aluminum, vehicle parts heavily tariffed).
Trade represents only 0.6% of Maryland GDP and 1.5% of Texas GDP; tariff drag limited relative to total economic output.
stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield's tariff exposure analysis found that Canada's retaliatory tariffs (exceeding $20 billion in response to Section 338 tariffs) disproportionately affect states with import-heavy compositions in tariffed products. Maryland, Kentucky, Texas, and Michigan face above-average tariff-related exposure due to reliance on automotive, vehicle parts, and aluminum imports. However, trade accounts for only 0.6% of Maryland's GDP and 1.5% of Texas' GDP, limiting the economy-wide drag.
stories.impact: Tariff-induced cost pressures could elevate construction material and labor costs (particularly in auto/supply-chain-dependent regions like Michigan and Texas) by increasing input expenses for building materials, equipment, and services. However, modest trade GDP contribution in most states suggests tariff impact on multifamily development feasibility will be marginal absent escalation. Monitor labor cost inflation and material availability in tariff-exposed regions; consider pricing escalation clauses in longer-term construction contracts in Michigan, Texas, and Maryland markets.

stories.title: Watermark Capital Moves Forward With School-to-Resi Conversion in Crown Heights
stories.excerpt: The 42-unit residential conversion of a former Roman Catholic school at 560 Sterling Place in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, is well underway. Watermark Capital Group’s redevelopment project at the corner of Classon Avenue and Sterling Place is going ahead at a former school campus owned by its neighbor, St. Teresa of Avila Roman Catholic Church. Site plans addressed to 783 Classon Avenue, which shares a tax lot with 560 Sterling Place, were filed Thursday with New York City’s Department of Buildings. The filing details the vertical expansion of an existing building to include a 42,181-square-foot residence and a 57,449-square-foot community facility. Signatories for the recent permits tie ownership to the Catholic Church and Watermark. Watermark, through the entity 560 Sterling, previously obtained the site’s ground lease from St. Teresa of Avila, according to a memorandum of lease filed Tuesday. The document references an initial lease signed in April 2024 and later modified in June 2025. The Tuesday filing coincided with a $16.48 million construction loan for the leasehold provided to Watermark’s project by California-based lender Genesis Capital. Wolfe Landau, a founding partner at Watermark, signed for the developer on the memorandum of lease and the loan agreement. The developer’s office did not respond to requests for comment. St. Teresa of Avila’s former school campus, which spans Classon Avenue between Sterling Place and St. Johns Place was once home to Brooklyn Jesuit Prep Middle School. The school relocated to East Flatbush in 2020. The remaining campus buildings are now leased to the New York State Court Officers Academy, which lists its offices at 541 St. Johns Place. St. Teresa of Avila leaders announced in June 2025 that its own church at 563 Sterling Place would be closing its doors, citing financial strain, declining participation and a deferred, multimillion-dollar repair bill. bullets: Watermark Capital converting 42-unit residential project from former school, 560 Sterling Place, Crown Heights, Brooklyn.
DOB site plans filed (783 Classon Ave, shared tax lot); 42.2K SF residential, 57.4K SF community facility.
$16.48M construction loan secured on leasehold; ground lease from St. Teresa of Avila Church (MOL filed Apr. 2024, modified June 2025).
stories.summary: Watermark Capital Group is advancing a 42-unit residential conversion of a former Roman Catholic school at 560 Sterling Place in Crown Heights, Brooklyn (corner of Classon Avenue and Sterling Place). DOB site plans filed Thursday detail vertical expansion: 42,181 SF of residential space and 57,449 SF of community facility. Watermark secured a $16.48 million construction loan on a ground lease obtained from St. Teresa of Avila Church; the lease was originally executed in April 2024 and modified in June 2025.
stories.impact: Adaptive reuse of institutional/school assets in Brooklyn reflects sustained multifamily value creation in gentrifying submarkets (Crown Heights) despite higher basis from ground leases and community facility requirements. This project signals developer confidence in Brooklyn apartment demand and willingness to navigate complex leasehold structures and community benefit arrangements. Monitor similar school/institutional conversion opportunities in Brooklyn and NYC—they represent alternative acquisition paths in constrained land markets but require sophisticated lease/community negotiation expertise and longer development timelines.
